entities.summary: Marcus Antonius, commonly known in English as Mark Antony, was a Roman politician and general who played a critical role in the transformation of the Roman Republic from a constitutional republic into the autocratic Roman Empire. He served as one of the three leaders of the Second Triumvirate, alongside Octavian and Lepidus, and played a key role in the Battle of Philippi, which marked the end of the Roman Republic. Antony's relationship with Cleopatra VII of Egypt, the last active pharaoh of Ancient Egypt, has become legendary, with the two leaders forming a close alliance and having three children together. This alliance ultimately led to the downfall of Antony and his fellow triumvirate members, as Octavian declared war on Egypt and defeated Antony's forces at the Battle of Actium in 31 BCE. The following year, Antony took his own life to avoid capture, while Cleopatra followed suit, marking the end of the Roman Republic and the beginning of the Roman Empire. Antony's legacy has endured for centuries, with his name becoming synonymous with bravery, loyalty, and power.
